newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-Jan 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** The federal government is set to announce a package of incentives to jumpstart plans to usher in private players into the state-controlled field of telecom servivces, the Business Standard reports.
Major concessions in the package include a five-year tax
holiday for the projects, possible treatment of licence fees as capital expenditure and raising limits on external commercial borrowings, the paper says.

** The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has cleared applications of three foreign stock broking houses including Dresdner, Kleinwort Benson and Cazenove Securities, the Economic Times reports.
All three applications have been cleared on the grounds
that they have identifiable Indian broking houses as partners. Future applications are likely to be subjected to a policy review, the paper says.
** GE Capital Services, a unit of U.S.-based General Electric Co said on Tuesday it reached an agreement with India's SRF Ltd to buy a majority stake in SRF Finance Ltd.
GE Capital said the deal would require approval from the
government's Foreign Investment Promotion Board and market-regulator the Securities & Exchange Board of India.
SRF Ltd said that GE Capital Services would pay 53.50

rupees per share to buy a controlling stake in SRF Finance Ltd. The firm said it would use the approximately 480 million rupees raised from the sale of its 50.5 percent stake in SRF Finance to reduce its debt.
MARKETS:

** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.86/87 per dollar on Wednesday, dealers said. It is expected to move in a narrow range on Wednesday, the key factors determining the band being the extent of dollar demand from companies and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dealers said.
Leading stocks firmed up in kerb deals late on Tuesday
on growing speculation about government policy announcements expected this week, dealers said.
In late evening, Reliance was quoted at 282.0 rupees up
from Tuesday's official close of 280.50 rupees. ITC rose 12.0 rupees to 415.0 and TISCO 2.0 to 213.0 and SBI was up two rupees to 214.50.
** The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 41.46 points, or 1.16 percent, to 3,604.20
** The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index climbed 12.65 points, or 1.25 percent, to 1,021.80
** The Delhi index gained 6.38 points to 767.93
** The Madras index added 50.30 points to 3,412.17
** The Calcutta index lost 1.24 points to 459.66
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
